result.abstract: The lecture describes the larynx: its situation, nine cartilages, joints, ligaments, intrinsic and extrinsic muscles, internal compartments, histology, blood supply, lymphatic drainage and innervation. It then covers the physiology of phonation and clinical correlations including laryngeal nerve damage, laryngeal obstruction and vocal nodules.

concepts.name: Larynx
concepts.definition: The upper expanded part of the lower respiratory tract, modified for producing voice; an unpaired median tube of cartilages linked by joints, muscles and ligaments. In adults it extends from the upper thyroid cartilage at C4 to the lower cricoid at C6.

evidence.quote: The larynx is the upper expanded part of the lower respiratory tract, modified for producing voice, also called the organ of phonation
Larynx extends from the upper thyroid cartilage at C4 to the lower cricoid at C6; higher in children (C2 to C3)

concepts.name: Laryngeal cartilage
concepts.definition: One of the nine cartilages of the larynx: three unpaired and large (thyroid, cricoid, epiglottis) and three paired and small (arytenoid, corniculate, cuneiform).

evidence.quote: Nine cartilages: three unpaired (thyroid, cricoid, epiglottis) and three paired (arytenoid, corniculate, cuneiform)
The larynx is composed of nine cartilages, of

concepts.name: Thyroid cartilage
concepts.definition: Large unpaired laryngeal cartilage shaped like an open book, open backwards, with two vertical quadrilateral laminae and superior and inferior cornua; its upper border lies at the body of C4.

evidence.quote: Shaped like an open book, open backwards, with two vertical quadrilateral laminae

concepts.name: Cricoid cartilage
concepts.definition: Signet-shaped ring with a narrow anterior arch and a broad posterior lamina, at C6; the only cartilage that completely encircles the lumen of the larynx.

evidence.quote: A signet-shaped ring with a narrow anterior arch and a broad posterior lamina, at C6
This is a signet-shaped ring of cartilage

concepts.name: Epiglottis
concepts.definition: Unpaired cartilage shaped like a tennis racket, with a free superior base and an inferior foot inserting into the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage; its laryngeal side faces the vestibule and its lingual side the base of the tongue.

evidence.quote: Shaped like a tennis racket with a curved lower handle forming its foot
Shape: tennis racket with curved lower handle forming the foot of

concepts.name: Arytenoid cartilage
concepts.definition: Paired triangular pyramid about 15 mm high whose concave base articulates with the cricoid lamina and whose apex articulates with the corniculate cartilage; it bears the vocal process and the muscular process.

evidence.quote: The apex articulates with the corniculate cartilage, the concave base with the cricoid lamina

evidence.quote: Corniculate: on the apices of the arytenoids

concepts.name: Cuneiform cartilage

evidence.quote: Cuneiform: in the aryepiglottic fold

evidence.quote: the lateral angle bears the muscular process (insertion of the posterior and lateral cricoarytenoid muscles)
The lateral angle presents the muscular process

concepts.definition: Elliptical synovial joint uniting the base of the arytenoid with the upper edge of the cricoid lamina, reinforced by the posterior cricoarytenoid ligament; functionally the most important laryngeal joint, allowing rotatory and gliding movements of the arytenoid.

evidence.quote: An elliptical synovial articulation reinforced by the posterior cricoarytenoid ligament, uniting the base of the arytenoid with the upper edge of the cricoid lamina
Elliptical synovial articulation reinforced by the posterior

concepts.name: Cricothyroid joint
concepts.definition: Flat synovial joint, reinforced by ligaments, between the lower cornu of the thyroid cartilage and the lateral face of the cricoid; the cricoid tilts at it around a transverse axis.

evidence.quote: A flat synovial joint reinforced by ligaments, joining the lower cornu of the thyroid cartilage and the lateral face of the cricoid
Movements: tilting of the cricoid around

concepts.name: Thyrohyoid membrane
concepts.definition: Extrinsic membrane running from the upper edge of the thyroid cartilage to the lower edge of the hyoid bone, with a medial and two lateral thickenings.

evidence.quote: Thyrohyoid membrane: from the upper edge of the thyroid cartilage to the lower edge of the hyoid bone

concepts.name: Thyroepiglottic ligament
concepts.definition: Extrinsic ligament attaching the lower narrow end of the epiglottis to the posterior surface of the thyroid angle.

concepts.name: Hyoepiglottic ligament
concepts.definition: Extrinsic ligament connecting the posterior aspect of the hyoid with the anterior surface of the upper end of the epiglottis.

concepts.name: Cricothyroid ligament
concepts.definition: Fibroelastic ligament between the cricoid and thyroid cartilages; stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process it forms the vocal ligament, and with the cricoid it surrounds the infraglottic cavity.

evidence.quote: The cricothyroid ligament, stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process, forms the vocal ligament
The median cricothyroid ligament, between the cricoid and thyroid cartilages

concepts.name: Vocal ligament
concepts.definition: Intrinsic ligament formed by the cricothyroid ligament stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process of the arytenoid; with muscle it makes up the vocal cord.

evidence.quote: The cricothyroid ligament, stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process, forms the vocal ligament

concepts.name: Vestibular ligament
concepts.definition: Intrinsic ligament tense between the thyroid angle and the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid.

concepts.name: Intrinsic laryngeal muscle
concepts.definition: Muscle of the larynx that moves the arytenoids and vocal cords, classified by action as tensor, dilator or constrictor of the glottis; all are paired except the transverse arytenoid.

evidence.quote: All the intrinsic muscles are paired except the transverse arytenoid (interarytenoid), which is unpaired

concepts.name: Cricothyroid muscle
concepts.definition: Paired intrinsic muscle, the only one lying on the outer aspect of the larynx; it elevates the cricoid arch and lowers the thyroid cartilage, tensing the vocal cord, and is important for the tone and pitch of the voice.

evidence.quote: The cricothyroid is the only muscle lying on the outer aspect of the larynx
Action: elevation of the cricoid arch and lowering of the thyroid cartilage, tensing the vocal cord

concepts.name: Posterior cricoarytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: Intrinsic muscle inserting on the muscular process of the arytenoid; the only dilator of the glottis and the only muscle that abducts the vocal cords, letting air through the rima glottidis.

evidence.quote: Posterior cricoarytenoids are the only abductors: the safety muscles of the larynx
1. Posterior ericoarytenoids: abduct the vocal cords.

concepts.name: Lateral cricoarytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: Muscle inserting on the muscular process of the arytenoid; a constrictor of the glottis that adducts the vocal cords.

evidence.quote: Adduct the vocal cords | Lateral cricoarytenoids, transverse arytenoid
2. Lateral cricoarytenoids: adduct the vocal cords.

concepts.name: Transverse arytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: The only unpaired intrinsic muscle of the larynx, inserting on the posterior side of the arytenoid; it adducts the vocal cords.

evidence.quote: Transverse arytenoid is the only unpaired intrinsic muscle
3. Transverse arytenoid: adduct the vocal cords.

concepts.name: Thyroarytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: Muscle running from the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage to the arytenoid, described with superior and inferior parts; listed among the constrictors of the glottis and as the muscle that relaxes the vocal cords.

evidence.quote: Relax the vocal cords | Thyroarytenoid
3. Thyroarytenoid: relaxes the vocal cords,

concepts.name: Vocalis muscle
concepts.definition: The inferior thyroarytenoid or vocal muscle, running from the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage to the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid; it tilts the arytenoid forward and tenses the vocal cord.

evidence.quote: inferior thyroarytenoid or vocal muscle (from the reentrant angle to the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid), which tilts the arytenoid forward and tenses the cord

concepts.definition: Muscle ensuring laryngeal mobility, especially during swallowing: the elevators are thyrohyoid, mylohyoid and digastric, and the depressors are sternothyroid, sternohyoid and omohyoid.

concepts.definition: Lymphatics of the larynx are very rich in the supraglottic zone, thinner in the subglottic zone and absent at the vocal cords; the supraglottic region drains to the internal jugular chain, the infraglottic to pretracheal and paratracheal nodes and the internal jugular chain.

concepts.name: External laryngeal nerve
aliases: external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve

+ External branch - innervates cricothyroid m

concepts.name: Recurrent laryngeal nerve
concepts.definition: Branch of the vagus arising on the right at the base of the neck and on the left in the thorax; motor to all the intrinsic laryngeal muscles except the cricothyroid and sensory below the vocal folds.

evidence.quote: Recurrent laryngeal nerve supplies all intrinsic muscles except the cricothyroid, and sensation below the cords
From the vagus, on the right at the base of the neck and on the left at the thorax

concepts.name: Galen's loop

evidence.quote: through an ascending branch anastomosing with the superior laryngeal nerve: Galen's loop

concepts.name: Phonation
concepts.definition: The set of mechanisms allowing vibration at the free edge of the vocal fold, transforming aerodynamic energy into acoustic energy; the sound is then modified and filtered by the supralaryngeal air cavities.

evidence.quote: The set of mechanisms allowing vibration at the free edge of the vocal fold, transforming aerodynamic energy into acoustic energy

concepts.name: Acoustic parameters of the voice
concepts.definition: The three parameters that characterise the voice: frequency in Hertz, depending on the vibration speed of the vocal folds; intensity in dB, depending on the force of pulmonary expiration; and pitch.

evidence.quote: Voice parameters: frequency (Hz), intensity (dB), pitch

concepts.name: Subglottic pressure
concepts.definition: Air pressure below the glottis created by the expiratory blow from the lungs; it overcomes the resistance of the vocal cords.

evidence.quote: The expiratory blow creates a subglottic pressure that overcomes the resistance of the vocal cords
2. Infraglottic air pressure is generated by the exhaled air

concepts.name: Vibratory cycle of the vocal folds
concepts.definition: Three-step cycle of phonation: the folds close as the arytenoids come together, they open when subglottic pressure overcomes the muscular and elastic resistance and a puff of air passes, then the folds close again.

evidence.quote: 1. Putting into phonatory position: the folds close as the arytenoids come together
2. Opening: when the subglottic pressure overcomes the muscular and elastic resistance, a puff of air passes at high speed

concepts.name: Supralaryngeal cavity
concepts.definition: Air cavities above the larynx, with the pharynx and oral cavity as areas of particular enhancement, that filter and resonate the laryngeal sound and articulate it into vowels and consonants.

evidence.quote: The sound produced is immediately modified and filtered by the supralaryngeal air cavities to become vowels and consonants: the bucco-pharyngeal resonators
Filter role: resonance and enrichment of certain frequencies or suppression of others, with two areas of particular enhancement, the pharynx and the oral cavity

concepts.name: Vocal cord abduction
concepts.definition: Movement of the vocal cords apart, produced by rotation of the arytenoid at the cricoarytenoid joint so that the vocal processes rotate laterally, giving a wide diamond-shaped opening.

evidence.quote: Rotatory movement around a vertical axis, abducting or adducting the vocal cords

concepts.name: Vocal cord adduction
concepts.definition: Movement bringing the vocal cords together, produced by rotation of the arytenoid at the cricoarytenoid joint; the cords are kept adducted as the first step of voice production.

evidence.quote: Rotatory movement around a vertical axis, abducting or adducting the vocal cords
1. The vocal cords are kept adducted

concepts.name: Vocal cord tension
concepts.definition: Tightness of the vocal cords, raised by tilting of the cricoid at the cricothyroid joint and by the cricothyroid and vocalis, and relaxed by the thyroarytenoid.

evidence.quote: Tense: cricothyroid and vocalis. Relax: thyroarytenoid

concepts.name: Hyoid bone
concepts.definition: U-shaped bone above the larynx, joined to the thyroid cartilage by the thyrohyoid membrane; closely associated with the larynx but usually considered a separate structure.

evidence.quote: It is closely associated with the larynx but is usually considered a separate structure
Hyoid bone: the U-shaped bone above the larynx

concepts.name: Trachea
concepts.definition: Tube of C-shaped cartilage rings below the cricoid, joined to it by the cricotracheal ligament.

concepts.name: Laryngeal prominence
concepts.definition: Forward bulge formed where the two laminae of the thyroid cartilage meet in the midline.

evidence.quote: formed where the two laminae of the thyroid cartilage meet in the midline

concepts.name: Laryngeal incompetence
concepts.definition: Failure of the larynx to act as a sphincter at the inlet of the lower respiratory tract, so that food and fluid may be aspirated into the trachea.

evidence.quote: In laryngeal incompetence, food and fluid may be aspirated
Laryngeal incompetence: food and fluid may be aspirated into trachea

concepts.name: External laryngeal nerve injury
concepts.definition: Damage to the external laryngeal nerve, paralysing the cricothyroid and giving weakness of phonation from loss of its tightening effect on the vocal cords; especially noticeable in singers.

evidence.quote: External laryngeal nerve: weakness of phonation from loss of the tightening effect of the cricothyroid
Paralysis after an external laryngeal nerve lesion alters the voice significantly, especially noticeable in singers

concepts.name: Weakness of phonation
concepts.definition: A weak, monotone voice, described after external laryngeal nerve injury from loss of the tightening effect of the cricothyroid.

evidence.quote: External laryngeal injury (superior thyroid artery ligation): weak, monotone voice
weakness of phonation from loss of the tightening effect of the cricothyroid

concepts.name: Unilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy
concepts.definition: Damage to one recurrent laryngeal nerve, often accidental during partial thyroidectomy; the cord on the affected side lies in the paramedian position and does not vibrate, though the other cord usually compensates.

evidence.quote: unilaterally, the cord lies in the paramedian position and does not vibrate, though the other usually compensates
Unilateral recurrent nerve palsy: paramedian cord

concepts.name: Bilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy
concepts.definition: Damage to both recurrent laryngeal nerves; both cords lie in the paramedian position, with loss of phonation and difficulty breathing.

evidence.quote: bilaterally, both cords lie paramedian with loss of phonation and difficulty breathing
Bilateral: stridor, airway emergency

concepts.name: Combined bilateral recurrent and external laryngeal nerve injury
concepts.definition: Damage to both the recurrent and the external laryngeal nerves on both sides, paralysing all the intrinsic muscles so that the cords lie in the cadaveric position.

evidence.quote: If both recurrent and external laryngeal nerves are damaged on both sides, all the intrinsic muscles are paralysed
Bilateral with external nerve: cadaveric position

concepts.name: Cadaveric position of the vocal cords
concepts.definition: Position in which the vocal cords are further abducted and fixed because all the intrinsic muscles are paralysed.

evidence.quote: all the intrinsic muscles are paralysed and the cords are further abducted and fixed: the cadaveric position

concepts.name: Paramedian position of the vocal cord
concepts.definition: Position of a paralysed vocal cord between abduction and adduction, in which it does not vibrate.

evidence.quote: the cord on the affected side lies in the paramedian position, between abduction and adduction, and does not vibrate

concepts.name: Hoarseness
concepts.definition: Hoarse voice, listed with unilateral recurrent laryngeal palsy and said to follow a lung or mediastinal mass because of the long course of the left recurrent nerve.

evidence.quote: Unilateral recurrent laryngeal palsy (thyroidectomy, left-sided aortic or lung lesions): hoarse voice, cord paramedian
The long left course is why a lung or mediastinal mass can cause hoarseness

concepts.name: Stridor

evidence.quote: Bilateral: stridor, airway emergency

evidence.quote: If they are paralysed, the adductors take the upper hand and the person might die from lack of air
If posterior cricoarytenoids are paralyzed, the adductor

concepts.definition: Choking that follows when a foreign body enters the larynx because the explosive cough reflex of the very sensitive superior laryngeal mucosa is slowed or absent.

evidence.quote: The mucosa of the superior larynx is very sensitive, so a foreign body causes immediate explosive coughing. If that reflex is slowed or absent, choking follows

concepts.definition: Manoeuvre for a choking victim: from behind, with the hands in front of the epigastrium, one as a fist and the other over it, three or four abdominal thrusts are given upwards and backwards to squeeze residual air up and dislodge the foreign body.

conflicts.issue: The packet says the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve perforates the cricothyroid membrane and gives sensory innervation of the subglottic stage. Standard teaching is that the external laryngeal nerve is motor to the cricothyroid, and that sensation below the vocal folds comes from the recurrent laryngeal nerve, as the packet itself states elsewhere.

conflicts.issue: The packet gives two accounts of pitch: one says it depends on vocal fold accommodation but especially on the shape of the supralaryngeal cavities, another says pitch depends on the frequency of vibration. In standard teaching pitch corresponds to frequency, and the quality shaped by the resonating cavities is timbre.

notes: Slide 37 and slide 64 are heavily garbled by OCR; quotes from them are copied as they appear (for example 'Posterior ericoarytenoids').
The packet treats 'cricothyroid ligament', 'median cricothyroid ligament' and 'cricothyroid membrane' as the same structure; they are merged into one concept.
Vocalis is taken to be the 'inferior thyroarytenoid or vocal muscle'; the packet lists vocalis (tenses) and thyroarytenoid (relaxes) separately, so no part-of link was recorded between them.

Superior and inferior thyroid arteries, the vagus, partial thyroidectomy, the piriform sinus and the named individual extrinsic muscles are mentioned only in passing and were kept inside definitions rather than made concepts.

Left out as untested side material: the course of the left and right recurrent nerves under the aortic arch and subclavian artery (hy:7, deeper:2) and the narrow glottis and oedema in children (deeper:4).

findings.detail: The packet never describes one thyroarytenoid muscle 'with superior and inferior parts' running from the reentrant angle to the arytenoid; it lists a superior thyroarytenoid and an inferior thyroarytenoid (vocal muscle) as separate constrictors, and separately says 'thyroarytenoid' relaxes the cords. The definition merges them from outside knowledge, so its inferior part is the same muscle the result's vocalis concept says tenses the cord; the two quotes given state only the relaxing action.

findings.detail: The packet supports this, but standard teaching separates the median cricothyroid ligament (the anterior midline band between cricoid arch and thyroid cartilage, the site of cricothyroidotomy) from the lateral part, the conus elasticus or cricovocal membrane, whose free upper edge is the vocal ligament. The result gives 'median cricothyroid ligament' and 'cricothyroid membrane' as aliases of the structure that forms the vocal ligament, and this is not reported under conflicts.
